title: You Wouldn't Implode In The Mariana Trench

scenes.notes: Hold your breath. Just ten metres down, your ears ache,
because the pressure's doubled and squeezed your one breath to half,

scenes.notes: and the floor of the Mariana Trench is still almost eleven kilometres below you.
By thirty metres it's a quarter, your heart's slowing, and you're not floating anymore, you're falling,

scenes.notes: and at a hundred, your whole breath fits in a water bottle, so blood rushes into your chest to fill the space, and even trained freedivers can come up from here coughing blood,
and by two hundred and fifty metres, you're about as deep as anyone has ever gone on a single breath, so from here on, pretend you somehow still have air.
Relax. That was the easy part.

scenes.notes: One kilometre down, your breath is squeezed into a shot glass, and your ribs can't fold that small, so something gives, and you still haven't imploded.
Sperm whales hunt down here with ribs built to fold.

props.text: ~2 KM OF WATER ABOVE THE PEAK

scenes.notes: drop Everest in beside you and its peak is still underwater,
and you've been extremely not alive since roughly the shot glass,
